title.en: Storytelling project: a story with a purpose

es: Escribir una historia de 220 a 270 palabras con gancho, tensión, giro, recursos de énfasis y una reflexión final.

teaching.en: To hook the reader, the narrator opens in a concrete moment, such as the night she missed the last train.
teaching.es: Para atrapar al lector, la narradora abre con un momento concreto, como la noche en que perdió el último tren.
teaching.explanationEs: El gancho abre con un momento concreto, no con una explicación del tema. Narrator = narrador/a.
segments: To hook the reader, the narrator opens in a concrete
moment, such as the night she missed the last train.
teaching.audioText: To hook the reader, the narrator opens in a concrete moment, such as the night she missed the last train.

teaching.en: To build tension, foreshadow the danger with a clue and delay the answer: the station was empty, and then I heard footsteps.
teaching.es: Para crear tensión, anticipa el peligro con una pista y retrasa la respuesta: la estación estaba vacía y entonces oí pasos.
teaching.explanationEs: Foreshadow = anticipar sin revelar. Clue + delay: primero la pista y, más tarde, la explicación.
segments: To build tension, foreshadow the danger with a clue and delay
the answer: the station was empty, and then I heard footsteps.
teaching.audioText: To build tension, foreshadow the danger with a clue and delay the answer: the station was empty, and then I heard footsteps.

teaching.en: The narrator plants a plot twist: little did I know that the stranger would turn out to be my new teacher.
teaching.es: La narradora prepara un giro argumental: sin saber yo que el desconocido resultaría ser mi nuevo profesor.
teaching.explanationEs: Little did I know + que… anticipa un giro con inversión (did I know). Turn out to be = resultar ser.
segments: The narrator plants a plot twist: little did I know that
the stranger would turn out to be my new teacher.
teaching.audioText: The narrator plants a plot twist: little did I know that the stranger would turn out to be my new teacher.

teaching.en: For emphasis, use a cleft such as It was the silence that frightened me, or an inversion such as Never had I felt so relieved.
teaching.es: Para dar énfasis, usa una frase cleft como «Lo que me asustó fue el silencio» o una inversión como «Nunca me había sentido tan aliviado».
teaching.explanationEs: Cleft: It was + lo destacado + that. Inversión: Never had I + participio. Úsalas una o dos veces.
segments: For emphasis, use a cleft such as It was the silence that frightened
me, or an inversion such as Never had I felt so relieved.
teaching.audioText: For emphasis, use a cleft such as It was the silence that frightened me, or an inversion such as Never had I felt so relieved.

teaching.en: A vivid detail, such as a cold bench or the smell of coffee, helps to set the scene before any reflection begins.
teaching.es: Un detalle muy gráfico, como un banco frío o el olor a café, ayuda a situar la escena antes de que empiece cualquier reflexión.
teaching.explanationEs: Vivid detail: lo concreto vale más que un adjetivo general. Set the scene = situar al lector.
segments: A vivid detail, such as a cold bench or the smell
of coffee, helps to set the scene before any reflection begins.
teaching.audioText: A vivid detail, such as a cold bench or the smell of coffee, helps to set the scene before any reflection begins.

teaching.en: Looking back, it dawned on me that I had feared the wrong thing, and a closing reflection should say so plainly.
teaching.es: Mirando atrás, caí en la cuenta de que había temido lo que no era, y una reflexión final debe decirlo con claridad.
teaching.explanationEs: It dawned on me + that… abre el momento de comprensión. La reflexión final dice qué cambió en ti.
segments: Looking back, it dawned on me that I had feared the
wrong thing, and a closing reflection should say so plainly.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es el gancho más eficaz para abrir la historia de Mia?

choices.text: This story is about a night I spent in a foreign airport.
I still remember the exact second the departures board went blank.
Airports are busy places where many things can go wrong.

feedback.es: El gancho eficaz abre en un momento concreto («the exact second…»). Anunciar el tema o generalizar sobre los aeropuertos no crea curiosidad.

hint.es: Un gancho abre en un momento concreto; no anuncia el tema ni generaliza.

origin.text: Mia is drafting a story about a night in a foreign airport. Her teacher says: set the scene quickly, but begin in the middle of a moment rather than announce the topic.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo que más me inquietó fue el silencio.»

feedback.es: En la frase cleft con una cosa se usa that (o which) para introducir lo que se destaca: It was the silence that…

hint.es: Con cosas, no con personas, la frase cleft usa este conector.

origin.text: Everyone expected the narrator to fear the stranger. Yet what troubled her most was the silence of the empty station. In her draft she wrote: It was the silence ___ worried me most.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es el giro de este fragmento?

choices.text: The platform was empty although a train was expected.
The narrator waited for the last train alone at night.
The man who seemed a threat was returning her lost wallet.

feedback.es: El giro revela que quien parecía una amenaza en realidad ayudaba: cambia cómo entendemos lo anterior. Las otras opciones son la situación inicial.

hint.es: El giro cambia el sentido de lo que el lector creía.

origin.text: I waited for the last train. The platform was empty, and a man followed me along it. He turned out to be the station guard, carrying the wallet I had dropped an hour earlier.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nunca antes había oído una ciudad tan callada.»

answer.text: Never before had I heard a city so quiet

feedback.es: Never before al inicio exige la inversión: had + sujeto + participio.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada recurso narrativo con su función.

pairs.es: Abrir con un momento que despierte curiosidad
Dar una pista y retrasar la respuesta
Cambiar el sentido de lo leído hasta ahora
Anticipar sutilmente lo que ocurrirá después

feedback.es: Cada recurso cumple una función distinta: abrir, tensar, sorprender y anticipar.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué recurso usa la narradora.

choices.text: Foreshadowing: she hints at events before they happen.
A flashback: she returns to an earlier year of her life.
A reflection: she judges what she learned from the events.

feedback.es: «Little did I know» anticipa, sin detallar, que la carta tendrá consecuencias: es foreshadowing. No hay regreso al pasado ni balance final.

origin.audio: Little did I know that the envelope on my desk would change my year. I stared at it for a long minute, and then the phone began to ring. It was the same number that had called me three times that morning, and this time I decided to answer.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito da la autora solo sonidos aislados en este pasaje?

choices.text: To show that the narrator is calm and in full control.
To build tension by delaying what is really happening.
To describe the room in everyday, vivid detail.
To introduce a twist that changes the whole story.

feedback.es: Los sonidos sueltos y la cuenta hasta diez retrasan la explicación y aumentan la inquietud: crean tensión. La narradora no está tranquila (busca la puerta) y no hay giro.

origin.text: When the lights went out, nobody moved. Somewhere behind me, a chair scraped across the floor, then stopped. I counted to ten, slowly, and heard only my own breathing. It was the silence that made me reach for the door.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender el final sobre la narradora.

choices.text: That she now trusts strangers less than before.
That she now avoids travelling alone at night.
That she has changed a habit, not just lived through a night.

feedback.es: Pide ayuda antes y escucha la voz amable antes de imaginar el peligro: la experiencia cambió su costumbre. No confía menos en los extraños ni deja de viajar: lo que cambia es su hábito de callar.

origin.audio: Looking back, I realise the real problem was never the empty station or the man in the grey coat. It was my habit of expecting the worst, and of staying silent when I needed help. Since that night, I ask for help earlier, and I listen for the kind voice before I imagine the dangerous one. My sister says that I sound calmer now, and I think that she is right, although I still remember how cold the bench felt.

prompt.es: Completa: «Entonces caí en la cuenta de que no había hecho nada malo.»

feedback.es: It dawned on me that… es la expresión fija para un momento de comprensión repentina; el verbo dawn va con on.

origin.text: I spent the whole walk home angry with the man in the grey coat. Then it ___ on me that he had done nothing wrong and that I had been the one who was afraid.

prompt.es: Escribe tu historia de 220 a 270 palabras con gancho, tensión, giro, énfasis y reflexión.

answer.text: I still remember the night I missed the last train. I was a student, and I had spent the whole evening at a friend's birthday party in the next town. When I reached the station, the platform was empty and the clock showed midnight. My phone had no battery, and the nearest taxi was far away. I sat on a cold bench and tried to stay calm. It was not the dark that frightened me; it was the silence. Never had I heard a city so quiet. Then, behind me, I heard footsteps. They were slow, and they were coming closer. I held my bag tightly and did not look back. 'Are you waiting for the last train?' a voice asked. I looked up, and my heart stopped. The man in front of me was wearing a long grey coat, and he looked strangely familiar. He turned out to be Mr Duarte, my new science teacher, who lived two streets away. He smiled, offered me a lift and even gave me his phone charger. All the way home I kept thinking about how afraid I had been of a person who only wanted to help. Looking back, I realise that the real problem was not the empty station. It was my habit of expecting the worst and of staying silent when I needed help. Since that night, I ask for help earlier, and I listen for the kind voice before I imagine the dangerous one.

The man in front of me was wearing a long grey coat, and he looked strangely familiar. He turned out to be Mr Duarte, my new science teacher, who lived two streets away. He smiled, offered me a lift and even gave me his phone charger. All the way home I kept thinking about how afraid I had been of a person who only wanted to help. Looking back, I realise that the real problem was not the empty station. It was my habit of expecting the worst and of staying silent when I needed help. Since that night, I ask for help earlier, and I listen for the kind voice before I imagine the dangerous one.

The night I missed the last train began like any other. I was at a party in the next town, and I left too late. On the platform, the clock showed midnight and nobody was there. I sat down and waited, because my phone had no battery. What frightened me most was the silence. Then I heard footsteps behind me, slow and close. I did not dare to look. The lights were weak, and the wind moved some old paper along the ground. A voice said, 'Are you waiting for the last train?' I looked up, and there was my new science teacher, Mr Duarte, in a long grey coat. It turned out that he lived nearby, and he offered me a lift home. In the car we hardly spoke, but it was warm, and the radio played softly. I felt almost ashamed. I had been afraid of a man who only wanted to help. Looking back, I learned that I often expect the worst when I am alone. Never again will I stay silent when I need help.

feedback.es: Una historia completa abre con un gancho concreto, da una pista y retrasa la respuesta, revela un giro, enfatiza una vez o dos y cierra con una reflexión.

origin.text: Tema: la noche en que perdiste el último tren. Datos: fiesta en otra ciudad; estación vacía a medianoche; el celular sin batería; oyes pasos; el desconocido resulta ser tu nuevo profesor de ciencias, que te lleva a casa; lo que te asustó fue el silencio; reflexión: pedir ayuda no es debilidad. Incluye gancho, tensión, giro, énfasis (cleft o inversión) y reflexión final.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión retrasa más la revelación del hermano para crear tensión?

choices.text: I opened the door slowly. Nobody spoke. Then, in the half-light, I recognised my brother, smiling and, to my surprise, holding flowers.
I opened the door slowly. Nobody spoke. My brother was standing there, smiling, because he had come to apologise.
I opened the door and, to my surprise, it was my brother, who was smiling and holding flowers.

feedback.es: La versión con pausas, penumbra y retraso del reconocimiento mantiene el suspense. La que empieza con pausas revela al hermano de inmediato, y la tercera lo anuncia de golpe.

origin.text: Draft: I opened the door. My brother was standing there, smiling. He had come to apologise.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuál es el giro de la historia.

choices.text: Clara had hidden a contract from the director for months.
Her promotion, seen as a favour, was earned by a rescue nobody noticed.
The director lost his post because of Clara's report.

feedback.es: El giro cambia el sentido de la historia: lo que parecía favoritismo era un mérito que nadie vio. No se dice que Clara ocultara nada ni que el director perdiera su puesto.

origin.audio: Everyone at the office assumed that Clara had won her new post because she was the director's friend. She never explained herself. Months later, a report showed that she had quietly saved a big contract the year before, while the director was on holiday.

prompt.es: Completa: «Yo no sabía que aquella carta cambiaría mi vida.»

feedback.es: Little did I know es una fórmula fija de foreshadowing que lleva inversión: did + sujeto + verbo base.

origin.text: The letter looked ordinary, just a white envelope with a blurred name on it. Little did I ___ that it would change my life.
